title: The data is very preliminary, but Vulcan failure may not be due to BE-4 engines
gist: ULA's Vulcan return-to-flight launch failed due to low booster performance causing early, sub-orbital stage separation; preliminary data reviewed by two sources point to a vehicle-side propellant feed problem rather than the Blue Origin BE-4 engines themselves. The failure likely grounds Vulcan for at least six months, hitting the Space Force and Amazon Leo, while a BE-4 fault would also delay New Glenn and NASA's Artemis plans.

insights.claim: ULA said its Vulcan return-to-flight mission experienced low booster performance just after liftoff, causing stage separation at too low an altitude and velocity to reach orbit, while the Centaur V upper stage and solid rocket boosters performed nominally.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
